framework.reasoning: SIR implementation_assumptions (confidence 0.95) explicitly states the paper's reference implementation is TensorFlow ('We implement our model in Tensorflow', Appendix A). Per architecture-planning rules this explicit statement takes precedence over the CV-domain PyTorch default. We target modern TensorFlow 2.x (eager + tf.function, tf.GradientTape) rather than the original TF1.x graph/session API for maintainability, since the SIR only commits to the framework identity, not the specific API vintage. The user-requested TinyNeRF consumer-hardware variant is likewise TensorFlow-based in its official form (bmild/nerf tiny_nerf.ipynb), keeping the whole repo framework-consistent. YAML is sufficient for config management given the flat, non-nested hyperparameter surface of this model (no need for Hydra's composition features).

tensor_flows.name: NeRFMLP forward pass (single sample-point batch)
steps: for i in range(8): h = Dense(256, activation='relu')(h); if i == 4: h = concat([h, gamma_x], axis=-1)  → [N_pts, 256] (or 316 right after the skip concat, projected back to 256 by that layer's weights)

tensor_flows.name: Full two-pass render (ray batch -> pixel colors)
steps: pts_coarse = rays_o[:, None, :] + rays_d[:, None, :] * z_vals_coarse[..., None]  → [N_rays, 64, 3]
render_out_c = VolumeRenderer.composite(rgb_c, sigma_c, z_vals_coarse, rays_d)  → rgb_map [N_rays,3], weights [N_rays,64]
pts_fine = rays_o[:, None, :] + rays_d[:, None, :] * z_vals_fine[..., None]  → [N_rays, 192, 3]
render_out_f = VolumeRenderer.composite(rgb_f, sigma_f, z_vals_fine, rays_d)  → rgb_map [N_rays,3]
return render_out_f.rgb_map  (rgb_fine), plus render_out_c.rgb_map (rgb_coarse) retained for the loss

tensor_flows.name: Training step (photometric loss + Adam update)
steps: with tf.GradientTape(): outputs = NeRFModel.render_rays(batch_rays_o, batch_rays_d, near, far, training=True)
loss_dict = PhotometricMSELoss()(outputs.rgb_coarse, outputs.rgb_fine, target_rgb)  → total_loss = ||rgb_coarse-target||^2 + ||rgb_fine-target||^2, summed over the 4096-ray batch

risk_assessment.description: SIR flags implementation_assumptions confidence 0.65, largely driven by the TinyNeRF consumer-hardware adaptation, which is sourced from an external community/author notebook rather than the peer-reviewed paper text and has unverified exact hyperparameters (image res, MLP depth, iteration count).
risk_assessment.mitigation: Isolated behind utils/tiny_variant.py as an explicitly swappable config preset (--tiny CLI flag) that never touches the paper-faithful default path; document TinyNeRF settings as best-effort estimates pending direct notebook inspection in a later stage if exact fidelity is required.

risk_assessment.description: Exact total training-step count (SIR ambiguity: 100k-300k range, defaulted to 250k) and the exact exponential LR decay rate are not pinned down in the paper.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Expose num_training_steps and lr decay endpoints as top-level config values (not hardcoded), so a user can sweep/match a specific reported PSNR by adjusting steps; document the assumed formula lr = lr0 * (lr_end/lr0)^(step/total_steps) in config comments.

risk_assessment.description: Hierarchical importance sampling's inverse-CDF ('sample_pdf') procedure is a well-known but numerically fiddly custom op (must correctly handle zero-weight bins, boundary clamping, and stop-gradient on the coarse network's weights per common practice, though the paper does not explicitly state stop-gradient).
risk_assessment.source: sir.json mathematical_spec — 'Coarse-network ray-color weights / hierarchical sampling PDF' (confidence 0.9), architecture module HierarchicalSampler (confidence 0.9)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Implement sample_pdf with an epsilon-stabilized PDF/CDF and unit tests against a known analytic distribution; stop_gradient the weights feeding the sampler by default, exposed as a config flag in case exact paper behavior differs.

risk_assessment.description: Weight initialization scheme is unspecified in the paper (confidence 0.55 in SIR).
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use Keras Dense layer defaults (Glorot uniform), which is standard for this architecture family and matches widely-used community reproductions; flag as swappable via a config-level initializer string.

risk_assessment.description: COLMAP dependency for real-scene (LLFF) pose estimation adds a nontrivial system dependency and potential long-running preprocessing step outside the core model code.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Isolate in preprocess_llff.py and the Docker image's system_deps; synthetic datasets (which ship ground-truth poses) remain fully runnable without COLMAP for a fast smoke test.

risk_assessment.description: LPIPS metric requires a pretrained perceptual network (AlexNet/VGG weights); a maintained pure-TF2 LPIPS port is less standardized than the PyTorch original, risking a version mismatch with the paper's reported LPIPS numbers.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Pin lpips-tf2 version; if unavailable/broken, document a documented fallback of computing LPIPS in a small isolated PyTorch sub-environment purely for the evaluation script, keeping the main training stack pure TensorFlow.

risk_assessment.description: Full paper-faithful training (250k steps, batch 4096 rays, Nc+Nf=192 samples/ray, 800x800 or 1008x756 images) requires ~1-2 days on a V100-class GPU and will not fit meaningfully within a 4GB-VRAM consumer GPU budget without the TinyNeRF-style reductions.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Ship two first-class configs: configs/full_paper.yaml (paper-faithful, high-VRAM) and configs/tiny_consumer.yaml (TinyNeRF-inspired: single MLP, ~100x100 images, no hierarchical sampling, few thousand steps) so users self-select based on available hardware; document expected quality gap explicitly rather than silently degrading the paper-faithful config.
